@make-proposal-agent

RT-INSTRUCTION-TEST-004

Run a complete RoomTreasury proposal analysis for this synthetic project. Coordinate all four specialists using your updated instructions.

Client: PixelCraft Studio
Project: Business Landing Page
Proposed client price: $1,500
Deadline: 15 business days

Client brief:
- Five responsive pages: Home, About, Services, Portfolio and Contact.
- Contact form with email notifications.
- Portfolio displaying six projects.
- Basic SEO and performance optimization.
- Client supplies logo and written content.
- No CMS requirement specified.
- Hosting and domain costs are excluded from the stated price.

Preserve unknowns as questions or assumptions. Do not approve or authorize execution.

Generate the complete proposal package using the existing RoomTreasury schema.

finalReport.reportText:
@make-proposal-agent RT-INSTRUCTION-TEST-004-REQ — FINAL REQUIREMENTS SPECIALIST REPORT
Client: PixelCraft Studio | Project: Business Landing Page | Analysis only; no proposal, approval, financial record, or execution has occurred.

A. Executive Summary
PixelCraft’s confirmed brief requires a five-page responsive marketing website, a contact form with email notifications, a six-project portfolio, and basic SEO/performance optimization. A bounded five-page, six-entry portfolio listing is a reasonable proposed planning interpretation, but it is not confirmed that six standalone project-detail pages, a CMS, or content workflow are excluded. The client will supply a logo and written content, yet readiness, completeness, media rights, technical access, form decisions and the 15-business-day start trigger are unknown. Requirements are not ready for a final delivery commitment or budget approval; they are ready for a clarification-led proposal revision.

B. Confirmed Requirements
Evidence: owner project brief sw_0950e4b5ad9aec51bb5e5ffb670b4f37; coordinator assignment sw_c5ff4b6c068a446387cf9f693eb1a18e.
- Five responsive pages: Home, About, Services, Portfolio and Contact.
- Contact form with email notifications.
- Portfolio displaying six projects.
- Basic SEO and performance optimization.
- Client supplies logo and written content; delivery dates and completeness are not verified.
- Hosting/domain costs are excluded from the stated price.
- Proposed price: 150000 USD cents; it is not agreed or received revenue.
- Deadline target: 15 business days; no start trigger or calendar date is supplied.
- No CMS requirement is specified.

C. Proposed Requirements / assumptions requiring confirmation
- Baseline: one portfolio page containing six client-supplied project cards (title, image/media, short copy and agreed destination). This does not include six separate project-detail pages.
- CMS, client editing, migration, custom administration, integrations, media editing/hosting, copywriting, analytics/reporting, formal accessibility certification, ongoing SEO, maintenance and support are separate decisions—not confirmed exclusions.
- Form baseline requires a single agreed email destination, agreed fields, client-selected provider/routing, validation and agreed spam control. Privacy/consent/retention requirements cannot be inferred.
- One consolidated review/correction approach and defined change control are recommended, not confirmed.

D. Scope and Deliverables
Proposed deliverables:
1. Scope/content decision record: sitemap, six-project architecture, content readiness, form and acceptance decisions.
2. Responsive page designs/build for the five named pages.
3. Portfolio listing in the confirmed six-project model.
4. Contact form configured to the confirmed email destination.
5. Basic technical/on-page SEO and documented performance optimization work.
6. Review deployment, test evidence and agreed handover.
Proposed boundaries: the “Business Landing Page” label does not reduce the explicit five-page requirement. Hosting/domain are outside the stated price, but their owner, access, configuration work and recurring dependencies remain unknown.

E. Acceptance Criteria — proposed for client approval
- All five agreed pages are reachable through working navigation and contain approved supplied content.
- Portfolio presents six approved projects in the chosen architecture; any media/link fallback behavior is agreed and testable.
- At agreed mobile and desktop viewports, navigation, page content and form have no blocking layout/interaction defect.
- Form rejects invalid required fields, shows understandable validation feedback, and a valid test notification reaches the nominated email recipient.
- Each agreed indexable page has an agreed title, meta description and heading structure; links are checked; robots/canonical/sitemap/indexability configuration matches written launch instructions.
- For representative Home, Portfolio and Contact pages, record review date, URL, audit tool/profile, media/request observations and before/after metrics where measurable; address confirmed avoidable oversized media or unnecessary blocking scripts.
- Keyboard/focus/form-label/error-message smoke checks are included. This is not an accessibility certification.
No ranking guarantee, numeric performance score, browser matrix, accessibility level, legal certification or uptime SLA is stated.

F. Missing Information — questions, impact and gates
Blocking before scope/budget proposal:
- Do six projects mean portfolio cards only, six detail pages, or another model? Affects page count, templates, content, SEO, QA, timeline and estimate.
- Is CMS/client editing, migration, or an integration required? Affects platform, access, effort and support.
- What exact form fields, recipient email, provider, spam control, error/success behavior and privacy/consent/retention decisions apply? Affects form deliverable and acceptance.
- What does “basic SEO/performance” include, and what test profiles/thresholds or launch/indexability decision apply? Affects acceptance and feasibility.
- Who is the client requester/acceptance authority; what is revision/change control; when are logo/content/six portfolio assets and rights evidence complete? Affects scope, schedule and acceptance.
- Who owns hosting/domain/DNS, bills ongoing providers and supplies safe deployment access? Affects launch dependency even if costs are excluded.
Blocking before build: approved scope/architecture, complete content/assets/rights, platform/access and form decisions, named feedback/acceptance contacts.
Blocking before launch: verified email notification delivery, production domain/indexability decision, completed agreed test record and client acceptance.

G. Scope Changes
No prior approved scope or proposal revision is evidenced for RT-INSTRUCTION-TEST-004. Consequently, there is no approved baseline to overwrite. Any move from six cards to detail pages, CMS, editing workflow, added integrations, content production, additional revisions or expanded SEO/performance work is added/modified proposed scope and requires re-estimation and client confirmation.

H. Dependencies and Timeline
Sequencing: clarification/content readiness → design/build → form/SEO/performance configuration → review/QA → client acceptance/launch. The 15-business-day target is conditional, not a commitment: it needs a declared start trigger, complete content and six portfolio assets, rights confirmation, hosting/domain/form access, booked delivery capacity, a named approver and agreed feedback timing. No calendar milestone can be derived from current evidence.

I. Risks and Concerns
- High scope risk: six projects may imply detail pages/CMS. Mitigation: written architecture decision before estimate.
- High dependency risk: logo/written content supply is confirmed in principle, not ready or complete. Mitigation: asset/content checklist and gate.
- High form risk: notification destination/provider/privacy choices unknown. Mitigation: client decision plus receipt/invalid-submission test.
- Medium-high schedule risk: no start trigger, capacity, feedback window or launch date. Mitigation: conditional milestone plan after gates.
- Medium quality risk: basic SEO/performance is undefined. Mitigation: approve the above protocol; do not claim an invented score or ranking.
- Medium cost/external dependency risk: hosting/domain costs are excluded but provider responsibility, access and recurring charges are unresolved. Mitigation: document payer/owner and operational dependency without treating costs as included.

J. Cross-Agent Findings
No RT-INSTRUCTION-TEST-004 findings from challenge, commitment intelligence, or treasury were available when this report was prepared. I therefore make no attribution regarding risks, existing obligations, resource conflicts, cost, margin or financial feasibility. The coordinator must incorporate those agents’ actual reports separately.

K. Recommendations
1. Obtain the architecture/CMS decision and a six-project content/rights inventory first.
2. Confirm form routing/provider, notification recipient, privacy/consent/retention decisions and spam control.
3. Define the SEO/performance review protocol and agreed launch/indexability choice; add thresholds only if expressly agreed.
4. Confirm hosting/domain/DNS access, provider/billing ownership, start trigger, feedback timing, acceptance authority and change control.
5. Send the clarified scope to treasury for independent estimate/feasibility and to commitment intelligence for obligation/resource checks; the 150000-cent figure remains proposed only.

L. Final Requirements Decision
NEEDS_CLIENT_CLARIFICATION. The explicit feature set supports a bounded planning proposal with transparent assumptions, but architecture, content readiness, form/provider/privacy, technical access, quality boundaries and schedule prerequisites materially affect scope, effort and acceptance. Do not authorize delivery, represent the price as agreed revenue, or treat any proposed exclusion as client acceptance.

Confidence: High for extraction of the confirmed brief and its omissions; medium for the proposed boundaries because the client has not confirmed them.

specialistReports.conclusion: Five pages govern over landing-page label; six-card/no-CMS model unapproved. Content supply not evidence of readiness; scope/form/quality/start gates remain.

finalReport.reportText:
@make-proposal-agent RT-INSTRUCTION-TEST-004-RISK — FINAL INDEPENDENT CHALLENGE REPORT
Client: PixelCraft Studio | Project: Business Landing Page | Test analysis only
Final recommendation: NEEDS_MORE_INFORMATION. The brief supports discovery and bounded planning, but it is not ready for execution, pricing acceptance, financial approval, commitment, reservation, or settlement.

A. Executive Assessment
The confirmed scope is five responsive pages—Home, About, Services, Portfolio and Contact—with a six-project portfolio, contact-form email notifications, and basic SEO/performance work. The 15-business-day deadline is not a commitment because no start trigger, calendar date, asset-readiness evidence, technical platform, access, staffed capacity or feedback schedule exists. The 150,000-USD-cent figure is a proposed client price, not agreed or received revenue; no delivery budget, ledger balance, commitments, reservations or policy evidence was supplied. I requested Treasury’s PixelCraft-specific cost/margin model directly (message sw_c3c40114047f492bbbe9b64da2763d6c); it was unavailable at the time of this report, so no numerical feasibility finding is made.

B. Scope and Requirements Challenges
1. “Business Landing Page” conflicts with the explicit five-page brief only if treated as a one-page deliverable. The five named pages control; do not reduce them to one page without written client confirmation.
2. “Portfolio displays 6 projects” does not establish cards versus six detail pages, external links versus hosted media, filtering, video embeds, or CMS/content-editing. Each alternative changes effort, QA, hosting and maintenance.
3. “Basic SEO and performance optimization” has no approved definition, threshold, browser/device matrix, analytics requirement, accessibility target, indexability choice or ranking guarantee.
4. “Client supplies logo and written content” does not establish completeness, quality, delivery date, project metadata, media, rights, approved copy or revision responsibility.
5. No CMS requirement is stated; this is a decision gap, not authority to assume static delivery or exclude CMS effort.
6. Form notifications require fields, recipient mailbox/CRM, provider, authentication, spam controls, error handling, retention/privacy wording and acceptance tests.

C. Delivery and Technical Feasibility
Fifteen business days could be a conditional elapsed-time target for a tightly bounded static implementation only after prerequisites and staffed handoffs are confirmed. It is not supportable today. Critical-path gates are: complete approved content/assets and six project records; portfolio architecture; CMS/platform; hosting/domain/DNS and deployment access; form-notification configuration; named client approver and feedback SLA; agreed test/launch conditions. Detail pages, CMS, incomplete assets, media processing, provider access delays or review cycles require a revised schedule and estimate.

D. Commitment and Effort Review
No confirmed commitment, assigned-resource record, reservation or cost estimate was provided. The proposed price cannot substitute for effort evidence. Potential—not confirmed—cost/liability areas include form/email delivery, anti-spam, media/CDN or external portfolio hosting, paid template/plugins, consent/privacy tooling, analytics, support, and maintenance. Hosting/domain are explicitly excluded from the stated price, but their provider, access, billing owner and deployment effect are still unknown. Treasury owns numerical estimation under the assigned role; its received model must be challenged for inclusion of discovery, design, content integration, deployment, QA, handover, revisions and contingency.

E. Financial Review
Verified/provided inputs: proposed client price = 150,000 USD cents; delivery budget = not established; price is not agreed or received.
Unavailable: actual rate, hours, base cost, contingency, overhead, taxes, payment fees, external-service costs, commitments, settled spend, configured budget and available funds.
Accordingly, projected margin and available funds cannot be calculated. Available-funds verification is incomplete because no authoritative project ledger was supplied. Do not interpret the proposed price as funding, approval, a project budget, or an authorization.

F. Evidence and Verification
• Owner/client context: sw_0950e4b5ad9aec51bb5e5ffb670b4f37.
• Coordinator’s exact risk assignment and boundaries: sw_ed7a689343a44acf89aecbb12a102cd7.
• Treasury financial-assignment context: sw_ecb11b4c88c745df89d29d6bbd30203c.
• Direct request for Treasury’s model: sw_c3c40114047f492bbbe9b64da2763d6c.
No authoritative backend record was accessed. Project identity beyond this synthetic correlation, requester/recipient eligibility, current revision, duplicate records, commitments, settled spending, policies and ledger data are unverified.

G. Risk Register
R1 | Scope/portfolio architecture | Critical | High | Cards, details, CMS, filtering and media model alter effort, schedule and ongoing cost. | Client confirms one architecture and exclusions; re-estimate any alternative. | Research + Design.
R2 | Schedule/dependencies | High | High | Missing start gate, assets, access, capacity and feedback timing make 15 days unreliable. | Dated prerequisite checklist, staffing plan and feedback SLA before publishing dates. | Research.
R3 | Content/assets/rights | High | High | Late/incomplete copy, six-project media or unclear rights blocks build or creates rework/legal exposure. | Content/rights manifest, quality criteria and approval date before design freeze. | Research.
R4 | Form notification/security | Critical | Medium | Undefined routing, provider/authentication, privacy, spam and failure behavior can lose enquiries or mishandle data. | Define fields, destination, provider/data ownership, spam control and successful/invalid/failed delivery tests. | Development + QA.
R5 | SEO/performance acceptance | High | High | Vague “basic” work creates an acceptance dispute or unpriced optimization. | Agree checklist/test method for metadata, links, indexability, media loading and representative mobile/desktop observations; no invented scores/rankings. | QA.
R6 | Platform/deployment | High | Medium | CMS, host, DNS, account ownership and rollback path are unknown, delaying release or adding work. | Confirm platform, access, billing owner, deployment and rollback responsibilities. | Development.
R7 | Financial viability | Critical | High | Price is only proposed and no cost model/budget exists; margin/funding cannot be assessed. | Treasury issues independent model; owner verifies terms, funding, external costs and capacity. | Treasury + Owner.
R8 | Maintenance/hidden costs | Medium | High | Form/email, anti-spam, media, plugins, updates, monitoring and support may become unpaid obligations. | Document provider, renewal, payer, warranty/support boundaries and failure owner. | Research.
R9 | Change control | High | Medium | No revision cap or acceptance authority enables uncontrolled rework. | Written review windows, change process and named approver. | Research.
R10 | Quality gap | High | Medium | Removing QA to meet a deadline risks non-working notifications, poor responsive behavior or avoidable performance issues. | Preserve form delivery, responsive, representative portfolio-media, SEO checklist and deployment/acceptance testing. | QA.

H. Revision Comparison
Not applicable. No prior PixelCraft baseline, approved budget, agreed price, or delivery revision was supplied. Nova/Apex figures and assumptions were deliberately excluded.

I. Cross-Agent Disagreements
No substantive PixelCraft specialist response was available when this report was completed. The only identified role dependency is Treasury’s forthcoming cost model; its financial conclusions have not been assumed.

J. Required Actions
1. Client/Coordinator: select portfolio architecture; CMS/static decision; six-project content/media/rights package; form-routing/privacy/provider choices; SEO/performance/QA acceptance boundaries; revision and acceptance authority.
2. Client/technical owner: provide hosting/domain/DNS, platform and deployment access plus billing/maintenance ownership.
3. Treasury: deliver PixelCraft-only independent cost, contingency, external-cost and hypothetical-margin model; re-review if scope changes.
4. Commitment Intelligence: verify any existing obligations, resource conflicts, duplicate commitments and unpriced liabilities from authorized sources.
5. Owner: verify commercial terms, capacity, funding/ledger facts and any later approval path. No action is authorized by this report.

K. Final Recommendation
NEEDS_MORE_INFORMATION for proposal completeness, delivery feasibility and financial viability; formal execution authorization is unavailable. A future PASS_WITH_CONDITIONS would require every critical gate above plus an independently challenged Treasury model. This is not an approval.

L. Confidence
High in the identification of scope/dependency/acceptance gaps because they are absent from the provided brief. Low in cost, margin, available-funds and resource conclusions because authoritative financial and capacity evidence is absent.

@treasury-ops-agent @make-proposal-agent RT-INSTRUCTION-TEST-004 — TARGETED CHALLENGE RECONCILIATION OF TREASURY MODEL (interim; no financial action)

Evidence: Treasury’s model, sw_dd09b45d8f3c4f5286f0119bd8e30313; source brief/assignment, sw_ed7a689343a44acf89aecbb12a102cd7.

Arithmetic check: internally consistent.
• Planning hours: 5 + 10 + 23 + 8 = 46.
• Base: 14,000 + 28,000 + 64,400 + 22,400 = 128,800 cents.
• Contingency: 25,760 cents is 20% of base; budget = 154,560 cents.
• Hypothetical margins versus the proposed—not agreed or received—150,000-cent price are correct: low +25,680 (17.12%); planning -4,560 (-3.04%); high -38,160 (-25.44%).

Material challenge
1. The baseline is conditional, not a quote-ready scope: client content/logo availability and usability are expressly unverified. A six-entry static listing, no CMS/details/integrations/content production and ready providers are assumptions that require client confirmation.
2. The 46h planning budget already exceeds the proposed price by 4,560 cents before excluded external costs, overhead, taxes and fees. Repricing or a separately specified reduced scope is required; a positive low-case calculation does not establish viability.
3. Research (5h) and QA/handover (8h) are vulnerable to being consumed by ordinary discovery/launch work. Identify whether the existing work includes: deployment configuration and rollback ownership; client review/correction allowance; form sender authentication/provider setup; valid/invalid/failed submission and inbox-receipt tests; responsive checks; representative six-project media/fallback tests; basic SEO/indexability checks; performance observations; handover. If excluded, add explicit scope/estimate; do not fund them silently from contingency.
4. “Standard email-notification form” is not sufficiently defined. Recipient, provider, authentication, spam control, data/privacy responsibility, error path and notification failure handling must be decided before build. These are execution gates, not inferred legal requirements.
5. The 15-day average of 3.07 productive hours/day is not a feasibility proof. Serial handoffs and client review create elapsed-time risk. Require pre-start assets/access, booked capacity by phase, named approver, written feedback windows, no CMS/detail-page expansion, and confirmed launch date before treating it as a target.
6. Preserve minimum safeguards in any lean scenario: form delivery/invalid/failure tests; agreed mobile and desktop responsive checks; portfolio media/fallback check; metadata/headings/link/indexability checklist; documented representative performance observations; deployment/acceptance sign-off. No score/ranking/accessibility-certification guarantee should be implied.

Conclusion: The model is a reasonable conditional planning hypothesis, but it is NOT READY FOR OWNER APPROVAL OR EXECUTION. Financial recommendation remains NEEDS_MORE_INFORMATION / re-scope or reprice after client scope and provider decisions, verified cost/capacity/funding facts, and explicit treatment of excluded recurring costs.

RT-INSTRUCTION-TEST-004 — Treasury’s addendum resolves the under-scoping question by making the 46h baseline explicitly conditional and preserving minimum QA/form/deployment safeguards. No arithmetic correction is needed; the 15-day target and 154,560-cent model remain conditional, and execution stays blocked pending the listed gates.

RT-INSTRUCTION-TEST-004 — Independent check: the itemized workstream hours reconcile exactly to 46h, and the stated base, contingency, total and proposed-price margin remain correct. The explicit boundaries and non-use of contingency for routine work resolve the requested control clarification; the financial and execution-blocked decision is unchanged.

specialistReports.conclusion: Independently confirmed46h model and arithmetic; explicit ordinary-work coverage resolves under-scoping concern only with ready content/providers. Reprice/re-scope; preserve minimum QA and conditional15-day target.

@make-proposal-agent RT-INSTRUCTION-TEST-004-COMMIT — FINAL COMMITMENT & RESOURCE INTELLIGENCE REPORT
Analysis only. No financial or resource record was created, changed, approved, reserved, or settled.

A. Executive Summary
I found no evidence of an existing payment promise, vendor agreement, invoice, approved resource reservation, completed delivery work, or backend-recorded commitment for PixelCraft Studio’s Business Landing Page. The brief establishes requested delivery features and a proposed client price, but neither establishes a financial obligation or available funding. Several potential unpriced liabilities and delivery dependencies are evidenced by the brief—particularly form/email notifications, hosting/domain exclusion, content readiness, portfolio media, potential templates/CMS, and support—but their supplier, amount, billing owner, and agreement status are unknown. Investigation status is INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE / POTENTIAL_COMMITMENTS_IDENTIFIED (unverified leads only); no project execution or approval should rely on them.

B. Financial Commitment Findings
1. Proposed client price: 150000 USD cents. Classification: UNVERIFIED_LEAD, not revenue, receivable, budget, or commitment. It is explicitly proposed and not agreed or received. Recipient/payer, payment terms, date, invoice, and owner approval are unknown.
2. Hosting and domain: the brief says costs are excluded from the stated price. Classification: EVIDENCE_FOUND for an exclusion, not for any client payment or vendor contract. Vendor, amount, renewal, account owner, and payer are unknown.
3. Contact-form email notifications: UNVERIFIED_LEAD for possible form/email, spam-control, transactional-email, privacy/consent, or inbox-delivery service obligations. No provider, pricing, contract, billing owner, recipient, data-retention terms, or payment promise is evidenced.
4. Templates/CMS: no CMS requirement is stated; this is not evidence that no CMS, template license, plugin, or editing workflow is needed. Any paid theme/template/plugin or CMS hosting is an UNVERIFIED_LEAD, not an existing liability.
5. Portfolio media: six project displays may require media hosting/CDN, image/video rights, optimization or license costs. Classification: UNVERIFIED_LEAD. No media host, license, rights proof, vendor, cost, or contracted service is in evidence.
6. Support/maintenance: no warranty, monitoring, update, or post-launch support term is stated. There is no current support obligation; future support is an UNVERIFIED_LEAD only.

C. Resource Commitment Findings
- Client content contribution: the brief states that the client supplies a logo and written content. This is a stated delivery dependency, classified PROPOSED_RESOURCE_ALLOCATION / unverified client responsibility. Delivery dates, completeness, rights, format, approver and acceptance status are unknown.
- Internal delivery resources: no named designer, developer, QA role, contractor, hours, assignment, reservation, utilization record, or work already performed was supplied. No CONFIRMED_RESOURCE_RESERVATION, AGREED_RESOURCE_ALLOCATION, or COMPLETED_RESOURCE_WORK was found.
- Deadline: 15 business days is a target without a start trigger or dates. It is not evidence of booked capacity or an agreed delivery reservation.

D. Evidence Register
- Owner project brief: sw_0950e4b5ad9aec51bb5e5ffb670b4f37. Supports the five-page requirement, form/email notifications, six-project portfolio, basic SEO/performance, client-supplied logo/content, unspecified CMS, excluded hosting/domain costs, proposed price, and 15-business-day target.
- Coordinator assignment: sw_d7aa315da968481a860fe4dd9752ca3a. Establishes the investigation scope and confirms that the 150000-cent price is not agreed or received, client content timing/completeness is unverified, and no prior-project assumptions may be carried over.
- No authorized read-only backend source, contract, invoice, purchase order, resource calendar, vendor account, ledger entry, project record, reservation, or attachment was supplied or accessible.

E. Verification Status
No CONFIRMED_COMMITMENT exists in the available evidence. No AWAITING_OWNER_CONFIRMATION workflow or backend record is evidenced. The identified payment/service/resource items are UNVERIFIED_LEAD or EVIDENCE_FOUND only, as specified above. Backend recording status for every potential item: unknown.

F. Duplicate and Conflict Findings
No possible duplicate financial commitment was found because no commitment records, recipients, invoices, amounts beyond the proposed client price, or source agreements are available. No resource conflict can be assessed because no assignments, reservations, working periods, or other-project capacity data were supplied. The five-page scope versus the “Business Landing Page” label is a naming/scope clarification issue, not a duplicate commitment.

G. Scope Revision Impact
No prior scope, vendor agreement, internal reservation, or completed work is evidenced, so no cancellation/change obligation can be identified. If a CMS, portfolio details, content production, paid template, media service, form/email provider, or support term is later added, it may introduce new financial and resource obligations; none should be presumed covered by the proposed price or existing resources.

H. Financial and Delivery Implications
The potential liabilities above are not costed or funded here; treasury owns financial estimation. They can affect eventual cost, timeline and margins, but no available-funds impact can be asserted. The 15-day target is exposed to unverified logo/content delivery, media rights/availability, provider setup, form routing/privacy decisions, and unreserved internal capacity.

I. Unresolved Questions
- Who, if anyone, agreed to the proposed 150000-cent price, under what payment milestones, and can the owner provide the contract/invoice/payment evidence?
- Which party owns and pays for hosting, domain/DNS, form/email delivery, spam protection, privacy/consent tooling, media/CDN, template/plugins and support?
- Is a CMS, editable portfolio workflow, detail pages, paid template, or premium plugin required?
- When will complete logo, copy, six portfolio records/media and rights evidence be delivered, and who confirms completeness?
- Which resources are actually assigned or reserved for the 15-day period, and do they conflict with other work?
- What backend project/request/revision, ledger, commitment/reservation and approval records exist, if any?

J. Recommendations
1. Make Proposal Agent should preserve all identified items as unverified dependencies, not allocations, commitments, or client-funded costs.
2. Owner/client should confirm commercial acceptance, payer/billing owner for each external service, content/rights readiness, CMS/portfolio model, and support boundaries.
3. Treasury should assess financial exposure only after providers, pricing, rate/capacity and payment terms are evidenced.
4. Challenge Agent should treat missing resource reservation, provider ownership and content readiness as blockers to a 15-day execution claim.
5. Before any later authorization workflow, obtain authorized backend read-only evidence for project/request revision, ledger commitments, reservations, balance/policy controls and owner approval.

K. Confidence and Limitations
Confidence is high that no confirmed existing obligation or reservation is evidenced in the supplied sources; it is medium that the listed service categories are relevant exposure areas. Confidence is low about actual liabilities, funding, duplicates and capacity because no backend, contract, vendor, invoice, calendar, or ledger access was available.

L. Final Investigation Status
INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and POTENTIAL_COMMITMENTS_IDENTIFIED (unverified service and resource leads only). NO_MATERIAL_CONFIRMED_COMMITMENTS_FOUND in available evidence. The proposal is not ready to treat any payment, revenue, allocation, resource capacity or vendor service as committed.

specialistReports.conclusion: No confirmed obligations/reservations evidenced. Forms/email, media, plugins, hosting exclusion and support are potential leads. Actual liabilities, duplicates and resource conflicts unknown without ledger/contracts/calendar.

@make-proposal-agent RT-INSTRUCTION-TEST-004-FIN — FINAL SPECIALIST FINANCIAL REPORT
Client: PixelCraft Studio | Project: Business Landing Page | Analysis only; no approval, commitment, reservation, record, or settlement occurred.

A. Executive Financial Summary
The proposed client price is 150,000 USD cents; it is neither agreed nor received revenue. My independent PixelCraft-only planning estimate is 154,560 cents including contingency, exceeding that proposed price by 4,560 cents before overhead, taxes, payment fees, and unpriced external services. The estimate is thus financially unviable under the stated planning assumptions, while the low scenario is only conditionally viable. Recommendation: reprice or reduce/document scope before any owner-review path; do not treat the proposed price as funding.

B. Revenue Structure
- Proposed project price: 150,000 USD cents.
- Contractually agreed revenue: unknown; recommend agreedRevenueCents: null in existing schema fields.
- Received revenue: unknown / zero evidence.
- Payment milestones, collection terms, taxes and deductions: unknown.
Hypothetical margins below use the explicit proposed-price basis only.

C. Cost Breakdown
Unverified PixelCraft-specific blended rate: 2,800 USD cents/hour.
- Research: 4–6h; planning 5h; base 14,000 cents. Scope/content/asset/provider discovery, requirements and launch plan.
- Design: 8–12h; planning 10h; base 28,000 cents. Responsive visual/page/component treatment and six-card portfolio presentation.
- Development: 19–28h; planning 23h; base 64,400 cents. Five pages, responsive implementation, six provided entries, email-notification form, basic technical SEO/performance work.
- QA/handover: 6–10h; planning 8h; base 22,400 cents. Responsive/form/notification, representative portfolio/media, SEO/performance checks, corrections and handover.
Base total: 46h / 128,800 cents.

D. Budget Allocation
Separate 20% contingency: 25,760 cents. Proposed planning limits (not reservations):
- Research 16,800 = 14,000 base + 2,800 contingency.
- Design 33,600 = 28,000 + 5,600.
- Development 77,280 = 64,400 + 12,880.
- QA 26,880 = 22,400 + 4,480.
Arithmetic: 16,800 + 33,600 + 77,280 + 26,880 = 154,560 cents; bases total 128,800 and contingency totals 25,760. Proposed delivery budget: 154,560 cents. These are planning limits only, not ledger reservations or authorized spend.

E. Commitment Reconciliation
Evidence classifications:
- Brief-supported prospective internal work: five pages, six-project portfolio, email-notification form, SEO/performance; source sw_0950e4b5ad9aec51bb5e5ffb670b4f37 and task assignment sw_ecb11b4c88c745df89d29d6bbd30203c.
- Potential obligations: internal delivery labor and unknown external services; unverified leads only.
- Backend-recorded commitments, reservations, settled spending, available balance, policy result and approval limit: UNVERIFIED. No authorized read-only backend evidence was available; do not subtract potential obligations from any balance.

F. Financial Scenarios
All calculations include the stated contingency and use proposed 150,000-cent price only:
- Lean/low delivery: 37h × 2,800 = 103,600 base + 20,720 contingency = 124,320 total; hypothetical margin 25,680 cents / 17.12%. Conditions: client-ready complete content/logo, static six-card portfolio, no CMS/detail pages, available provider access, bounded revision/testing.
- Planning baseline: 46h / 128,800 base + 25,760 contingency = 154,560 total; hypothetical margin −4,560 cents / −3.04%.
- Downside: 56h × 2,800 = 156,800 base + 31,360 contingency = 188,160 total; hypothetical margin −38,160 cents / −25.44%.
These exclude external/recurring costs and overhead; none establishes profit or cash availability.

G. Margin Analysis
Projected gross margin = proposed price − estimated delivery cost.
At the baseline: 150,000 − 154,560 = −4,560 cents. Because cost already exceeds the proposed price before excluded costs, this project should not be called profitable or financially viable. The contingency may not be used to absorb ordinary unscoped work; it must be separately governed.

H. Scope Revision Impact
There is no prior PixelCraft approved baseline to compare. No Apex or Nova rates, budgets, allocations, revenues, or scope assumptions were used. Material scope additions—CMS, portfolio detail pages, content remediation/creation, custom integrations, richer media processing, analytics/reporting, formal accessibility/performance targets, or support—require re-estimation, revised contingency and proposed-price revision.

I. Missing Information
Client/content dates and completeness; portfolio information architecture and rights; CMS/platform; email notification provider, inbox, spam and privacy/retention decisions; hosting/domain access (cost excluded, but readiness unknown); revision/change-control rules; launch/acceptance authority; actual internal rate/capacity; external-service prices/billing owner; payment milestones/taxes; and authoritative backend balance/commitment/reservation/policy/approval evidence.

J. Risks, Dependencies and Recommendations
- Margin deficit — Critical: baseline exceeds proposed price. Reprice or reduce scope after client confirmation.
- Schedule/capacity — High: 46h over 15 business days averages 3.07 productive hours/day but assumes sequential resources are booked, prerequisites exist at start, and client feedback is timely. Treat 15 days as conditional, not committed.
- Form/security/provider — High: email routing, spam, privacy and delivery tests can add cost or block launch. Confirm before build.
- External exposure — High: hosting/domain are excluded, while form/email, anti-spam, consent/privacy, media/CDN, analytics, premium templates/plugins, payment fees, taxes, overhead and support are unpriced. Identify payer and costs.
- Scope ambiguity — Critical: lack of a CMS requirement does not exclude CMS; six projects may require only cards or a deeper architecture. Obtain written client decision and change control.
Send the model to the owner only as a planning recommendation, not an authorization. Before any future simulated financial operation, require a current request/revision, independent policy result, backend-verified human approval, authoritative funds/commitments/reservations, explicit simulation permission and receipt/ledger reconciliation.

K. Independent Challenge Coordination
I sent the numeric model and focused under-scoping questions to challenge-agent for independent review: sw_dd09b45d8f3c4f5286f0119bd8e30313. No challenge response had been received at the time of this final report; any material correction should trigger a targeted reconciliation addendum rather than treating this estimate as settled.

Confidence
Medium in the arithmetic and conclusion that the planning baseline exceeds the proposed price. Low in actual cost, capacity, revenue realization and external-cost exposure because core assumptions remain unverified.

Financial Readiness Decision
FINANCIALLY_UNVIABLE_UNDER_CURRENT_ASSUMPTIONS. The planning baseline requires repricing or a client-confirmed scope reduction and re-estimation; it is not ready for approval or execution.
